questions.question: Which language should the browser game use?
questions.rationale: A browser-based game is the requested target; TypeScript is recommended for its game-state and renderer code.

questions.question: Which rendering approach should the game use?

options.label: Custom Canvas raycaster
options.description: Build the classic first-person raycasting renderer directly on Canvas.

options.label: Phaser
options.description: Use a 2D game framework for input, scenes, and rendering.

options.label: Three.js
options.description: Use a 3D engine for a fully 3D implementation.

questions.rationale: A custom Canvas renderer best matches the requested Doom-style raycasting experience, while leaving room to choose a framework.

questions.question: What platform and controls should the game support?
questions.recommendedChoice: Desktop browser with keyboard and mouse (WASD + mouse look)
questions.rationale: Desktop keyboard-and-mouse controls are a practical default for a first-person raycasting game; confirm or specify other platforms.

questions.question: What scope and mechanics should the first version include?
questions.recommendedChoice: A compact playable prototype with movement, collision, and one small level; no combat unless requested
questions.rationale: A small, complete level keeps the first playable build focused while making the core movement and exploration testable.

questions.question: What visual style and asset approach do you prefer?
questions.recommendedChoice: Retro pixel-art textures and a restrained original sci-fi palette using generated or simple original assets
questions.rationale: Original retro-inspired assets capture the era without depending on copyrighted Doom assets.

questions.question: Should the first deliverable be a playable first-person raycasting prototype?
questions.rationale: The raycasting view is the defining mechanic implied by the game request.

questions.question: Which data stores does the project need?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Keep the game client-side with no persisted player data.

questions.rationale: The initial browser game can run entirely client-side without persistence.

questions.question: Will users sign in to access application features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users sign in to access application API features.

options.label: No
options.description: The game is playable without an account.

questions.rationale: No account or API-backed feature was requested.
